column1: # What a finished machine has, checked by .scripts/machine-check.sh. Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-22-complete-provisioning-design.md, section 1.
# Columns (tab-separated): id, machines (all, a known_hostnames name or research_host), by (script: provisioning does it, you: Michael does it), step, verify.
# Row order is the order to do things in. A verify is read-only, never prompts and ends well inside 30 s. "-" means no check (you rows only).
# A verify runs as `env -i` with only HOME, USER, LOGNAME, XDG_CONFIG_HOME, XDG_DATA_HOME, XDG_CACHE_HOME, XDG_STATE_HOME, MACHINE, DOTFILES (the source
# under /usr/bin/timeout -k 5 30 /bin/zsh -f -c, with the working directory $HOME and stdin /dev/null. tests/provisioning.test.sh lints this file.

column4: ComputerName and HostName are the machine's name (the preflight sets them)
Everything in the Brewfile is installed
Every marketplace and plugin in ~/.config/agents/plugins.conf is installed (re-run dotfiles-run reconcile-agents when not)
Homebrew zsh is the login shell
Oh My Zsh is in the XDG data folder
Every mise tool is installed
The application firewall is on
The Claude Code managed policy is the repository's

Every be.netronix.* LaunchAgent in ~/Library/LaunchAgents is loaded, or disabled with launchctl disable (one the loader reports not in the source is a leftover: launchctl bootout it and delete its plist)
column5: p=("$HOME"/Library/LaunchAgents/be.netronix.*.plist(N)); (( $#p )) && for f in $p; do launchctl print "gui/$(id -u)/${f:t:r}" >/dev/null 2>&1 || launchctl print-disabled "gui/$(id -u)" | grep -F "\"${f:t:r}\"" | grep -q 'disabled$' || exit 1; done

column4: The native ssh agent holds its two keys, michael and viumore_rsa
column5: s="$HOME/.local/state/ssh-agent/agent.sock"; l=$(SSH_AUTH_SOCK="$s" ssh-add -l) && for k in michael viumore_rsa; do f=$(ssh-keygen -lf "$HOME/.ssh/$k.pub" | awk '{print $2}'); [ -n "$f" ] && [[ $l == *"$f"* ]] || exit 1; done

column4: ssh to GitHub authenticates
column5: SSH_AUTH_SOCK="$HOME/.local/state/ssh-agent/agent.sock" ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=10 -o ControlPath=none -o UpdateHostKeys=no -T git@github.com 2>&1 | grep -q 'successfully authenticated'

column4: ssh to GitLab authenticates
column5: SSH_AUTH_SOCK="$HOME/.local/state/ssh-agent/agent.sock" ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=10 -o ControlPath=none -o UpdateHostKeys=no -T git@gitlab.com 2>&1 | grep -q 'Welcome to GitLab, @'

column4: NetBird's root daemon is installed and running
provision.sh joins NetBird with the setup key in 1Password's "NetBird setup key" (fallback: netbird up and the SSO login)

provision.sh generates Syncthing's config before its first start: the GUI login from 1Password's "Syncthing GUI"; Global Discovery, Relaying and NAT traversal off, Local Discovery on (fallback: section 8 E1 by hand)
column5: C="$HOME/Library/Application Support/Syncthing/config.xml"; x() { xmllint --xpath "string($1)" "$C"; }; [ -n "$(x //gui/user)" ] && [ -n "$(x //gui/password)" ] && [ "$(x //options/globalAnnounceEnabled)" = false ] && [ "$(x //options/relaysEnabled)" = false ] && [ "$(x //options/natEnabled)" = false ] && [ "$(x //options/localAnnounceEnabled)" = true ]

column4: The Herdr plugins dev.phase, dev.agent-rows and smart-splits.nvim are linked
column5: o=$(herdr plugin list 2>/dev/null) && for id in dev.phase dev.agent-rows smart-splits.nvim; do print -r -- "$o" | grep -q "^- $id " || exit 1; done

column4: provision.sh hands Vorta this machine's profile, the export in 1Password's Document "BorgBase <machine>" (fallback: this machine's BorgBase repository and a schedule, set up in Vorta)
column5: [ "$(sqlite3 -readonly "$HOME/Library/Application Support/Vorta/settings.db" "select count(*) from backupprofilemodel where repo_id is not null and schedule_mode != 'off'")" -ge 1 ] && [ ! -e "$HOME/.vorta-init.json" ] && security find-generic-password -s vorta-repo >/dev/null 2>&1

column4: The be.netronix.login-apps LaunchAgent opens Syncthing, Vorta, Alfred and the menu-bar apps at each login (its list: Library/LaunchAgents/be.netronix.login-apps.plist)

The Codex daemon runs a pinned copy of the CLI's package; provisioning pins a fresh machine only, so otherwise, when no review is active: "$(codex-daemon real-bin)" app-server daemon update --from-cli, then, if you use the herdr TUI, ./tests/run.sh live-codex-daemon (AGENTS.md)
column5: [[ "$(readlink "$HOME/.codex/packages/app-server-daemon/current")" == */releases/local-* ]] && real=$(codex-daemon real-bin) && v=$("$real" app-server daemon version 2>/dev/null) && { [ "$(print -r -- "$v" | /usr/bin/jq -r .status)" != running ] || print -r -- "$v" | /usr/bin/jq -e '.cliVersion == .appServerVersion'; }

column4: No system sleep, wake for network access, restart after power loss
chezmoi renders hercules' Borg key, ~/.ssh/borg-hercules
chezmoi renders fenrir's Borg keys and the huginn key, ~/.ssh/borg-fenrir, borg-append-only-fenrir and huginn
Leave 1Password, Settings, Developer, "Use the SSH agent" off; the native agent serves ssh
column5: for s in "$HOME/Library/Group Containers/2BUA8C4S2C.com.1password/t/agent.sock" "$HOME/.1password/agent.sock"; do [ -S "$s" ] && /usr/bin/nc -U -w 1 "$s" </dev/null >/dev/null 2>&1 && exit 1; done; true

column4: Start claude once in a terminal or Herdr pane of the desktop login and sign in (from an SSH login Claude Code cannot write the keychain and keeps the login in plain text, in ~/.claude/.credentials.json; delete that file after signing in again)
Start codex once in a plain terminal, not a Herdr pane, and sign in
gh auth login, glab auth login and az login
column5: /usr/bin/timeout 10 gh auth status >/dev/null 2>&1 && glab auth status >/dev/null 2>&1 && AZURE_LOGGING_ENABLE_LOG_FILE=false AZURE_CORE_COLLECT_TELEMETRY=false az account show >/dev/null 2>&1

column4: Open OrbStack once, so it installs its helper
Open Alfred and enter the Powerpack licence
System Settings, Privacy and Security, Accessibility: add Alfred (without it the snippets expand nothing)
Run dotfiles-run configure from your terminal: it turns on snippet expansion and restarts Alfred to index the relay snippets (it may ask for Automation consent)
column5: A="$HOME/Library/Application Support/Alfred"; h=$(/usr/bin/jq -r .localhash "$A/prefs.json") && [ -n "$h" ] && [ "$(defaults read "$A/Alfred.alfredpreferences/preferences/local/$h/features/clipboard/prefs" autoExpandSnippets)" = 1 ] && [ "$(sqlite3 -readonly "$A/Databases/snippets.alfdb" "select count(*) from snippets where collection='Relay'")" -ge 1 ]

column4: Open Little Snitch and allow its network extension
column5: systemextensionsctl list | grep -i littlesnitch | grep -q 'activated enabled'

column4: Enter the Little Snitch licence, then add the rules of hercules-agent-machine section 8 G (netbird, Syncthing, hercules' sshd)
Only if hercules joined with SSO: NetBird dashboard, Peers, hercules, Session Expiration off (section 8 B3)
column5: s=$(netbird status --json 2>/dev/null) && print -r -- "$s" | /usr/bin/jq -e '.daemonStatus == "Connected" and .management.connected == true and (has("sessionExpiresAt") | not)' >/dev/null

column4: On a reinstalled machine: delete its old peer in the NetBird dashboard, then put its new NetBird IP in the other machine's Syncthing address for it (section 8 E2) and, for hercules, in the SSH config note (section 2)
On a reinstalled machine, remove this machine's old device ID on the peer (it has a new one)
Pair with the peer again, add the three folders of section 8 E3 to E5; claude-memory stays Receive Only until Up to Date, then Send and Receive
column5: C="$HOME/Library/Application Support/Syncthing/config.xml"; x() { xmllint --xpath "string($1)" "$C"; }; f() { local d; d=$(x "//folder[@id=\"$1\"]/@path"); [ "${d/#\~/$HOME}" = "$HOME/$2" ] && [ "$(x "//folder[@id=\"$1\"]/@type")" = "$3" ] && [ "$(x "count(//folder[@id=\"$1\"]/device)")" -ge 2 ]; }; f claude-memory .claude/projects sendreceive && [ "$(x '//folder[@id="claude-memory"]/versioning/@type')" = staggered ] && f "codex-memory-$MACHINE" .local/state/codex-memory-share/outbox sendonly && for peer in ${=KNOWN_HOSTNAMES}; do [ "$peer" = "$MACHINE" ] || f "codex-memory-$peer" ".local/state/codex-memory-share/inbox/$peer" receiveonly || exit 1; done

column4: Open the Herdr app, run ~/.config/herdr-app/bin/respaces with its window open, then pick the michael layout (cmd-shift-L)
Configure Spotlight privacy settings, grant each app the permission it asks for at first launch, and sign in to the apps that need an account
Turn on Remote Login and Screen Sharing (System Settings, General, Sharing)
column5: d=$(launchctl print-disabled system 2>/dev/null) && print -r -- "$d" | grep -Eq 'com\.openssh\.sshd.* enabled' && print -r -- "$d" | grep -Eq 'com\.apple\.screensharing.* enabled'

column4: Remote Login off, or on and key-only per security-locks-2 section 7 (your key in ~/.ssh/authorized_keys, a key login from the other Mac, then the 000-hardening.conf drop-in)
column5: d=$(launchctl print-disabled system 2>/dev/null) && [ -n "$d" ] && { ! print -r -- "$d" | grep -Eq 'com\.openssh\.sshd.* enabled' || { [ -s "$HOME/.ssh/authorized_keys" ] && c=$(/usr/sbin/sshd -G 2>/dev/null) && print -r -- "$c" | grep -qix 'passwordauthentication no' && print -r -- "$c" | grep -qix 'kbdinteractiveauthentication no' && print -r -- "$c" | grep -qix 'permitrootlogin no'; }; }

column4: Turn FileVault on (System Settings, Privacy and Security). On hercules, after a restart, unlock it over SSH from the home LAN, to its LAN address, with your account password (macOS 26 and later on Apple silicon, Remote Login on; NetBird is not up before unlock): the pre-boot unlock accepts the password although sshd is otherwise key-only. Then log in once at the desktop (Screen Sharing): the LaunchAgents and login items (the Codex daemon, Vorta backups, Syncthing) do not run until a desktop login; on hercules that login also moves Herdr's core into it (be.netronix.herdr-core-desktop), and Herdr panes opened before it stay in the SSH login, so reopen them; stay logged in there, ending a Screen Sharing session by disconnecting, never by logging out, since a logout may end Herdr's core and every pane

With hercules reachable over NetBird: run ssh hercules true once, comparing the host key with ssh-keygen -lf /etc/ssh/ssh_host_ed25519_key.pub on hercules (section 8 C); redo it after a hercules reinstall
column5: ssh -o BatchMode=yes -o ConnectTimeout=5 -o ControlPath=none -o StrictHostKeyChecking=yes -o UpdateHostKeys=no -o PreferredAuthentications=none hercules true 2>&1 | grep -q 'Permission denied ('

column4: Run hc machine add hercules (section 8 D)
First run under launchd: launchctl kickstart gui/$(id -u)/be.netronix.weekly-research, then read the note
column5: o=$(weekly-research --status) && print -r -- "$o" | grep -qx 'result: ok' && print -r -- "$o" | grep -qx 'vault inbox: writable'

column4: In a fresh Claude Code session run ./tests/run.sh live-agent-signing live-credential-boundary live-agent-auth; if you use the herdr TUI: start codex once in a TUI pane and clear its first-run screens, then, unsandboxed, ./tests/run.sh live-codex-daemon; with Remote Login on, ssh -o PubkeyAuthentication=no to this Mac from the other Mac must be refused
